_comment: pykonal_locext configuration. Paths must be absolute.
_traveltime_dir_help: REQUIRED. Grids are stored one HDF5 file per station-phase (NET.STA.PHASE.h5) in this directory, plus a small inventory.h5 master of external links that pykonal reads transparently.
_edt_ot_wt_help: NonLinLoc's LOCMETH EDT_OT_WT (default true). Each arrival implies its own origin time; at the true hypocentre these agree, and at a point that satisfies many differential times only by coincidence they scatter. The EDT pdf is therefore penalised by the weighted variance of those origin-time estimates, floored at log(1e-5). This compacts the location PDF without giving up outlier robustness, because the weights are the EDT pair probabilities themselves, a bad pick satisfies few pairs and contributes almost nothing. Set false for the plain EDT pair sum.
_edt_exponent_help: Exponent applied to the EDT stack. null (default) means the number of arrivals, which is what NonLinLoc uses. This is no longer a cosmetic choice: the EDT_OT_WT penalty is added after the power, so the exponent sets the balance between the two terms. Set a number only if you know why; 1 gives the raw, broadest EDT surface.
_alpha_help: Adds fractional per-arrival uncertainty proportional to its traveltime, e.g. 20 second traveltime * 0.02 = +0.4 sigma. 2% seems to work better than < 0.01, but adding more beyond this may actually hurt.
_default_pick_error_help: Per-phase default pick uncertainty (seconds; MUST be > 0). Event-level box sizing uses the smallest floor in the map. Keys may also be exact phase labels (e.g. "Sg": 0.2), which take precedence over the P/S entry for picks with that label.
_pick_error_help: Observation uncertainty in the EDT objective: each pick's variance is sigma^2 + (alpha * traveltime)^2, where sigma is the pick's own time uncertainty if it has one else default_pick_error (seconds, the fixed picking error), and alpha is a fractional model error that grows with traveltime.
_phase_map_help: Which arrival phase labels are located with. The traveltime grids hold FIRST-ARRIVAL times, so by default only first-arrival labels are used: P, Pg, Pn, Pb, P*, p (as P) and S, Sg, Sn, Sb, S*, s (as S), matched exactly and case-sensitively. Anything else (pP, sP, PmP, SmS, Lg, Rg, T, ...) arrives later than the grid predicts and is not located with; such arrivals stay in the output with weight 0 so the association is kept, and the log lists them. phase_map ({label: "P" | "S" | null}) is checked first: map a label your network uses for a first arrival, e.g. {"Pup": "P"}, or exclude a built-in one with null, e.g. {"P*": null}. null (the default) = the built-in list only.
_outlier_help: Iterative residual-based arrival rejection. After locating, arrivals whose residual deviates from the median by more than max(outlier_cutoff_s, outlier_mad_factor * MAD) are dropped and the event is relocated, up to 3 passes, never going below outlier_min_arrivals. The MAD term adapts to how noisy the event is; the absolute floor stops a very clean event rejecting picks that are only slightly worse than its excellent others. Rejected arrivals are NOT deleted from the output - they appear with weight 0 and timeUsed false so the analyst sees which were dropped, and the reported RMS is over the used arrivals (making it comparable to NonLinLoc). Set outlier_cutoff_s to 0 to disable. Note EDT already ignores such picks when locating so this mainly fixes reporting and removes competing likelihood modes.
_search_delta_auto_help: search_delta_km may be a [lat,lon,depth] list OR the string "auto" (recommended!). auto sizes the location search box per event as auto_search_k_sigma * the LARGER per axis of (a) the linearised prediction C=s^2(G^T G)^-1 from the traveltime gradients at the initial hypocenter (s from the measured residual rms) and (b) the sigma measured from a cheap provisional posterior (auto_search_posterior_nsamples) in a wide first-pass box. The result is raised to the floors (auto_search_min_km, auto_search_depth_dist_factor) then capped by auto_search_max_km. After locating, if the uncertainty estimate still runs into a HORIZONTAL edge of the box, that axis is widened automatically (up to auto_search_max_km, at most 3 passes) and resampled, so no manual tuning is normally needed; the log says when this happens. Depth is never widened: a depth posterior that reaches the box edge means the arrivals do not constrain depth, which is reported as a NOTE. auto_search_cond_max flags weak/degenerate-depth geometry above that condition number.
_auto_search_k_sigma_help: Half-width of the LOCATION search box in multiples of the provisional sigma. 4 is a good default. The uncertainty estimate no longer depends much on this, because a truncated horizontal axis is widened automatically afterwards; lower values make the location search denser, higher values make automatic widening rarer.
_auto_search_max_help: Cap on the auto half-widths [lat,lon,depth] in km, for both the location search box and the automatic widening of the uncertainty estimate. If the log warns that an axis is still understated at the cap, it prints the half-width that event needs; raise this value on that axis.
_auto_search_min_help: Absolute floor on the auto half-widths [lat,lon,depth] in km. With the search now seeded at the anchor rather than the box centre, a box that is too small no longer fails gracefully: the search cannot wander into a solution outside it, so an under-resolved sigma produces a confident location at the anchor. auto_search_max_km still overrides these.
_auto_search_depth_dist_help: Depth half-width floor as a fraction of the distance to the NEAREST contributing station. Heuristic: beyond roughly one focal depth the takeoff angle stops changing with depth and the arrival constrains origin time rather than depth, so depth is not resolvable much better than the nearest offset regardless of how small the residuals are. Set 0 to disable.
_auto_search_posterior_help: Samples used in the PROVISIONAL pass to measure the location sigma that sizes the real search box. 0 falls back to the linearised C = s^2 (G^T G)^-1 prediction, which assumes independent residuals and is optimistic (especially wrt depth) wherever the velocity model produces residuals that trend with distance. This is not the reported uncertainty; that is still posterior_nsamples.
_search_delta_help: Half-widths of the search box in km, in the order [north-south, east-west, depth], centred on search_anchor. NOTE this order differs from the internal grid axis order, which is [depth, north-south, east-west] for spherical grids. Only used when not "auto". Sizing rule for a fixed box: at least 6x the uncertainty you expect on each horizontal axis (EDT posteriors have heavier tails than a Gaussian; at 4x the reported sigma was measured about 10% short). A fixed box is never widened automatically: if the posterior reaches its edge the log prints a WARNING with a suggested search_delta_km.
_posterior_help: Samples used AFTER the location to characterize its uncertainty: the EDT likelihood is sampled once around the solution with scrambled Sobol (quasi-random) points drawn from a mixture of a Hessian-based proposal and a uniform component over the box. This builds the confidence ellipsoid and the lat/lon/depth uncertainties written to the origin and shown in scolv. Rounded up to a power of two. Run-to-run variation of the reported sigmas is about 1% at 4096, 1.5-2% at 2048 and 2-4% at 1024. The box is only a rejection boundary: an oversized box costs sampling density but cannot bias the result, while an undersized one truncates the pdf and understates the uncertainty. Truncation is detected directly (posterior density still high at the box edge): in auto mode horizontal axes are then widened automatically; otherwise the log prints a WARNING with a suggested box. The solution log reports 'ess=' (effective sample size); values below ~50 mean the uncertainty is poorly resolved --> raise this value. Set 0 to skip uncertainty estimation entirely. EDT only; ignored for method 'l1'
_search_anchor_help: Where to CENTER the search box (anchor +/- search_delta_km). 'origin' (DEFAULT, recommended) = the input origin. 'stations' = the centroid of the stations with arrivals, at default_depth. This makes the location a pure function of the picks (successive scolv relocations become idempotent, since scolv feeds each result back as the next initial origin), but it is sensitive to the box size in BOTH directions: the box must still reach the event from the network centroid (the search cannot leave it, and auto-sized boxes are capped by auto_search_max_km), yet a very wide box makes the search find the event blind and the sampling sparse, which does much worse. It suits a compact network with events inside it. scolv's 'ignore initial location' option (--ignore-initial-location) selects 'stations' for that run.
_posterior_seed_help: Fixed seed for posterior sampling, or null (DEFAULT) for independent draws each relocation. With quasi-random sampling the reported uncertainties vary only ~1-2% between seeds, so null is fine; set an integer if you need bit-identical output. The hypocentre itself does not depend on this.
_confidence_level_help: Confidence level in PERCENT for the reported uncertainties. 68 (default) matches NonLinLoc. The confidence ELLIPSOID is the three-dimensional region at this level (1.878 sigma at 68%), horizontalUncertainty is the two-dimensional horizontal region (1.515 sigma), and the per-axis latitude/longitude/depth uncertainties are one-dimensional marginals (1.000 sigma). Earlier versions emitted bare 1-sigma semi-axes labelled as a confidence ellipsoid, which made pykonal ellipsoids look about half the linear size of NonLinLoc's for the same posterior. Set 95 to report 95% regions instead.
_velocity_models_help: pykonal ScalarField3D HDF5 files per phase. Needed to compute traveltime grids; whether missing ones are computed is controlled by build_missing. Without velocity_models nothing can be built, and arrivals with no stored grid are reported with weight 0.
_build_missing_help: Compute absent traveltime grids before locating (default true). Any station/phase in the picks with no stored grid is solved once from velocity_models (one FMM solve, seconds to minutes) and persisted, so later runs and concurrent processes reuse it. Needs velocity_models and the station's coordinates from stations_csv (the ObsPy driver also accepts a station_inventory, merged with the CSV). false = locate with the grids that exist; arrivals without one get weight 0 and the log says which. Read by both pykonal_locext and pykonal_obspy; pykonal_obspy.relocate(build_missing=...) overrides it for one call.
_max_dist_km_help: Station-event distance limit (km), used for BOTH which arrivals are located with and how far each station's traveltime grid extends. Arrivals beyond it are excluded from the solve but kept in the output with weight 0. If the key is absent the default is 1000. null means NO limit and must be set explicitly: grids are then stored uncropped (the whole velocity model per station-phase), which costs far more disk and memory. Raising the value (or setting null) makes existing grids too small, so they are deleted and rebuilt automatically with a log message; run pykonal_prepopulate.py right after the change so this happens before relocations do. Lowering it keeps the existing grids, which cover the smaller range already. Zero and negative values are rejected.
_solve_n_closest_help: If > 0, solve the hypocenter using only the N geographically closest arrivals (ranked by epicentral distance from the initial origin), while STILL reporting a residual for every arrival and keeping them all in the output. Only the N solved-with arrivals are marked used (their input weight and timeUsed true); the farther ones get weight 0 and timeUsed false, and do not count towards the used-phase count or the azimuthal gap. Distant arrivals in a 1D model carry Pn/model error that can drag the solution; restricting the solve to nearby stations that sample the represented crust can sharpen the hypocenter without discarding the far arrivals from the output. Arrivals lacking station coordinates cannot be ranked and are always report-only. Outlier rejection still uses all residuals to decide what is bad but relocates on the closest set. 0 = use all arrivals to solve (default).
_depth_help: OPTIONAL physical bounds (km) on the depth search. depth_min = shallowest allowed (negative permits solutions above the datum, e.g. -1.0 allows 1 km above sea level); depth_max = deepest allowed. The anchor is NEVER moved: the search is restricted to the intersection of (anchor depth +/- search_delta_km[2]) and [depth_min, depth_max], expressed as an explicit asymmetric search interval, and the reported depth uncertainty is measured over the full unclamped extent. (Earlier versions recentered the box on the clamped interval, which walked the reported depth toward depth_min + half_width under scolv's repeated relocation.) Remove BOTH keys to disable clamping. You may set just one, e.g. only depth_max to cap depth while leaving the top open for station elevation.
_fixed_depth_tolerance_km_help: Search window (km) around --fixed-depth. The pin is enforced as this +/- window, not an exact value: the solver may place the depth anywhere inside it, and the REPORTED depth is the solved value - residuals, origin time and uncertainties all correspond to it - with an origin comment recording both the operator's pin and the solved depth. Set 0.001 for an effectively exact 1 m pin; the 2.0 default lets the data refine the operator's estimate within the stated tolerance, plus lets the user know which direction the depth prefers to go.
_ensure_nproc_help: parallel FMM solves when several grids are missing at once; null = min(n_missing, cpu_count), 1 = serial
_stations_help: CSV 'NET,STA,lat,lon,elev_m', read by both pykonal_locext and pykonal_obspy. Station coordinates are needed to build missing grids (build_missing), for max_dist_km and solve_n_closest, and for azimuthal gap and arrival distances/azimuths. The ObsPy driver merges it with a station_inventory passed to relocate(); the inventory wins for stations it contains, because it carries operating epochs. Stations with no coordinates still locate, without those features.
_log_arrival_detail_help: Log per-arrival distance, predicted traveltime, implied apparent velocity and residual. Use to diagnose large residuals: if apparent velocities exceed your velocity model, the traveltime grids were built from a model that is too fast. Note EDT locates on differential times, so a systematic traveltime error cancels in the hypocenter and is absorbed by the origin time - the location can match another locator while absolute residuals remain large.
_log_search_detail_help: Log the search-box sizing internals (floors, caps, measured/predicted sigma, depth-clamp arithmetic) and, after the uncertainty estimate, sigma, sampled half-width, edge density and fill for each axis. Off by default: the normal log shows one search-box line plus a WARNING or NOTE only when something needs attention.
